result.competitor: No Paraguayan product found that tracks Ley 5424 credentials or compliance. GeoVictoria has a Paraguay-localised page for security-guard attendance and rounds, so it covers part of the roster and attendance need. Foreign guard-tour and roster tools (OfficerReports, C-Guard Pro, SOVA, COREDINATE) cover patrols and shifts, not police credential or licence expiry, nor labour-proof packs for DNCP contracts. No free state portal for agencies was found (not checked in depth).
result.duty: Ley 5424/15 (Paraguay, in force), regulated by Res. Comandancia PN N°2 of 4 Jan 2016. The Policía Nacional's Departamento/División de Fiscalización de Empresas de Seguridad Privada y Afines licenses agencies and issues guard credentials ('carné de habilitación'/'carné de idoneidad'). Firms must notify the Policía 72 hours before event coverage. According to a tender Q&A, cash-transport firms hold 2 certificates that are valid for one year. DNCP tenders require a valid licence and often a real-time Sistema de Control de Guardias. Not confirmed: periodic personnel-list filings, renewal frequency for general guard agencies, and the penalty schedule (law text on BACN returned 403). Labour side (Jul 2026, abc.com.py): the Labour Minister calls security and cleaning outsourcers problematic and says DNCP will train contract administrators on labour law. A bill to bar sanctioned firms from bidding is only proposed. The Senate amendment working group in the Última Hora article dates from Aug 2023, so its current status was not reached.
result.market: Licensed agencies: about 252 in 2022 (La Nación/Hoy) and 135 in June 2023 after the police purged about 200 of 350 registrations. Police estimate about 300 operate unregistered. The Senator cited over 60,000 guards (2023). No 2025-2026 register count was found.
result.reason: The duty is real. Ley 5424/15 and Res. 2/2016 require a Policía Nacional licence and police-issued guard credentials, and firms must give 72 hours' notice before event coverage. DNCP tenders ask for a valid licence and a Sistema de Control de Guardias. I could not confirm a recurring periodic filing to the Policía (BACN text blocked). GeoVictoria (Paraguay page) and foreign guard-tour apps cover rosters and rounds, but none tracks Ley 5424 credentials. The "Senate bill under review" claim is stale: the Última Hora article is dated Aug 2023. The market is small (135-252 licensed firms), and many are informal, low-margin and resist compliance. Paying for compliance is driven mainly by state contracts. Pain and frequency are modest; demand is narrow.

coverage.found: Quarries: MOPC Viceministerio de Minas y Energia runs a Catastro de Canteras Web (about 151 licensed stone and lime quarries, article dated 23 Jan 2025). Permits needed: prior MADES environmental licence, municipal patente and Digemabel/Dimabel authorisation to buy explosives. Digemabel makes quarries file a plan de fuego, get approval, then declare use of each coded unit in its system (SID). After the Jun 2026 Santa Rita bank robbery, which used explosives declared as used at a quarry in Emboscada, Digemabel Res. 260/2026 (18 Jun 2026) set extraordinary controls: mandatory in-person oversight of each blast in Ita, Emboscada and San Lazaro, purchase restrictions, and scrutiny of declared-versus-actual use. Operators pay part of the fiscalisation cost (fuel and some military staff). The Senate (Jul 2026) is working on easing legal purchase while keeping control. Imports of explosives exceed 2,000,000 kg per year (2024), 98% going to quarrying, worth about G. 100,000 million. Intermediaries must register under Dimabel Res. 244/22. MADES environmental audit reports follow SEAM Res. 201/2015 and must be signed by a consultant in the CTCA register (Decreto 954/13); a general audit period for quarries or builders was not found. No MOPC contractor registry or category scheme found; the only contractor list is the DNCP supplier registry (SICP/IDAP), and CAPACO is a trade body. No Paraguay-specific construction-site safety rule from 2025-2026 found. General labour rules apply to builders: digital Libros de Informacion Laboral (MTESS Res. 462/2026, extension Res. 805/2026) and MIPYME contract registration (Res. 220/2026 under Ley 7444/2025). Sand and river-dredging permit rules not found (unverified).

result.competitor: The SIRO portal is free and run by the state, and it handles registration and ROS/RN filing. Three searches found no Paraguayan AML compliance software, kit, or outsourced compliance-officer service for jewellers, pawnshops or car dealers: one for software, one for PLA/FT risk-matrix software and one for outsourced compliance officers. The results showed only law-firm notes, compliance-officer training (a BNF/FOTRIEM certification programme), and an Argentine BDO risk tool aimed at banks. Local accountants and lawyers probably offer manual templates, but I did not verify this.
result.duty: Ley 1015/97 lists pawnshops and dealers in jewellery and precious metals as obligated subjects. SEPRELAD Res 375/2016 registers obligated subjects that have no natural supervisor. Res 222/20 is the AML/CFT rule for dealers in jewellery, stones and precious metals. It requires: tiered KYC (full KYC from 30 minimum salaries, about US$9,470; simplified KYC up to 50 minimum salaries a year); a senior compliance officer (the owner in a sole proprietorship); a manual and code of ethics; a risk assessment at least every 2 years; an annual internal review reported to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end; an external audit only above about Gs 9.2bn turnover; ROS filings, plus a negative report if no ROS is filed in 3 months; and 5-year record retention. Jewellers had to register or re-register in SIRO from 19 Sep 2022, and older certificates became void on 1 Jan 2023. In Feb-Mar 2023, SEPRELAD resolutions (numbers not given in the source) extended SIRO access and ROS/RN filing to pawnshops, vehicle importers/sellers/consignees, notaries, remitters and political organisations. For vehicle dealers, Res 196 sets the compliance officer rule. SEPRELAD has run random inspections since 2021 under Res 36/21. Penalty amounts were not found. All of this comes from Ferrere law-firm notes; I did not open the resolution texts.
result.market: Not found. There is no public count of jewellers, pawnshops or gold buyers registered in SIRO. Ferrere mentions that SEPRELAD runs a lookup module for its register of obligated subjects in SIRO, but I did not query it. The only related figure is from an older ABC article: 133 casas de crédito registered with SEPRELAD, which is a different category. I did not check whether a 'compro oro' segment exists. The likely total is low thousands at most across jewellers, pawnshops and vehicle dealers, but that is an estimate, not a verified figure.
result.reason: The duty is real, but I only saw it in law-firm summaries, not in the resolution texts themselves. Res 222/20 requires jewellers to keep tiered KYC (full KYC from 30 minimum salaries), appoint a compliance officer (the owner can do it in a sole proprietorship), write a manual and code of ethics, review risk every 2 years, and send SEPRELAD an annual internal-review report within 90 days. If no ROS is filed in 3 months, a negative report is due. SIRO registration has applied since 1 Jan 2023. In 2023, SIRO ROS/RN filing was extended to pawnshops and vehicle sellers. I found no local compliance-kit software. The quarterly negative report is trivial to file in the free SIRO portal. The real value is KYC records plus manual and matrix templates, which is close to consultancy. Market size was not found. Willingness to pay is likely low, and many of these firms are informal.

result.competitor: The only tools found are free state portals: the Abogacía del Tesoro/DGPEJBF registry and MEF SIARA. A Spanish search found no private software or gestoría packaging the annual BO update, forms A-E and the semiannual transparency page; accountants probably do it informally. I found no SaaS for the semiannual transparency publication.
result.duty: Ley 6446/2019 with Decreto 3241/2020: register beneficial owners and the legal entity within 45 business days, report changes within 15 business days, and update by 30 June every year. Fines of 50-500 jornales mínimos; ICNL also lists RUC blocking. Ley 7363/2024 (promulgated 15 Nov 2024) with Decreto 4806/2025: existing OSFL must register in SIARA (siara.mef.gov.py, live 1 Dec 2025) within 90 days, and new ones within 30 days. Every year by 30 June they file forms A-E with the DGPEJBF: activities, funding, staff, linked entities and a balance sheet. Every six months they must publish fund-use data on their own website, by the end of July and the end of January. Churches are excluded. Sports clubs, sindicatos, campesino groups, comisiones vecinales and juntas de saneamiento are covered only when they handle public funds for public policy. SEPRELAD registration of OSFL is still required under Ley 1015/97 as amended by Ley 3783/09. Not checked: Ley 7363 sanction amounts, the SIARA deadline actually set, and whether the Episcopal Conference got the extension it asked for. Constitutional challenges were filed (a second one in July 2026). A Senate bill to exempt comisiones vecinales has been postponed.
result.market: An ABC Color headline (July 2024) says the law would affect 10,000 comisiones vecinales; I did not open the article. No figures found for registered OSFL in SIARA or for associations in the BO registry (not reached). The likely paying segment is the smaller group of NGOs and foundations that receive public or donor funds, which ABC reports total over G. 56,000 million in the 2025 budget.
result.reason: Both duties are real. Under Ley 6446/2019, associations, sindicatos, juntas vecinales and similar bodies must update the register by 30 June each year, with fines of 50-500 jornales and RUC blocking. Ley 7363/2024 is now in force through Decreto 4806/2025 and the SIARA portal (live Dec 2025). It requires OSFL to file annual forms A-E (including a balance sheet) to the DGPEJBF by 30 June and to publish semiannual transparency data on their own website. Churches are exempt. Comisiones vecinales are covered only if they get public funds, and a Senate bill would ease their rules. The only tools I found are the free state portals; I found no private product. Weak points: legal challenges, volunteer buyers with little money, reaching them.

result.competitor: I found no vendor offering a full AML kit (manual, risk matrix, KYC files, ROS and negative reports, annual report, audit preparation) for car lots. Partial overlap: Compliance Paraguay, a local consultancy (La Nación, Aug 2024), sells a database of more than 9,000 politically exposed persons and explicitly targets car dealerships among other obligated firms. It is a screening-only tool, and the article does not say whether it handles manuals, ROS or annual reports. SEPRELAD's SIRO is a free state tool, but only for filing reports. Two other offers were seen but not checked: certification courses that train compliance officers (FOTRIEM/BNF) and law-firm advisory work (Ferrere). Neither CADAM nor CIVU templates were found.
result.duty: SEPRELAD Res 196 of 4 Sept 2020 is the AML/CFT rule for anyone importing, buying, selling or consigning motor vehicles, under Law 1015/97 as amended by Law 3783/09. It replaced Res 85/15. Última Hora dates the rule to 9 Sept 2020 (article fetched). It requires: a full AML/CFT prevention system with a manual and a code of ethics, a compliance officer, customer KYC with risk profiles and monitoring (a simplified route up to 15 minimum wages for single payments and 20 for instalment sales), suspicious-transaction reports (ROS) filed through SEPRELAD's SIRO system, a risk assessment at least every 2 years, an annual compliance-officer report due within 90 days of fiscal year end, and an external audit report due within 180 days. I found no repeal or replacement for 2024-2026, but I did not see the official text and did not confirm that the rule is still in force. I could not confirm the specific fines or any enforcement since 2020. The 2019 article mentions warnings to 704 firms and sanctions being announced.
result.market: Última Hora (2 Nov 2019) counted 1,142 used-car lots, of which 704 were warned and fewer than half filed ROS. Only 110 lots belong to CIVU. Another article in the same period says more than 700 firms and individuals own used-car lots, plus the CADAM importers (over 90 brands). I found no current register count. Roughly 700-1,200 obligated businesses, many informal.
result.reason: The duty is real, recurring (annual report, external audit, ROS and negative reports, risk review every 2 years) and specific to this sector. I found no tool that does the whole compliance job. Compliance Paraguay sells only a database for screening politically exposed persons, and SIRO is only for filing. Against it: there are only about 700-1,200 buyers, many of them informal and below half compliant. I could not confirm fines or current enforcement, so how much they would pay is uncertain. The external audit is a separate outside cost, and law firms and consultants probably already sell manuals. An MVP is simple (template manual, KYC forms, report calendar, risk matrix) and could later extend to other obligated firms without a sector supervisor (real estate, pawnshops, jewellers). Reachable through CIVU and CADAM.

result.competitor: The free SEPRELAD SIRO portal handles filing ROS and negative reports, but nothing else: no KYC records, risk matrix, manual or audit preparation. Two Spanish searches for SEPRELAD PLA/FT compliance software and outsourced compliance services found no Paraguayan SaaS for small obligated subjects. Training programmes for compliance officers exist (e.g. Fotriem/BNF certification), and law and accounting firms such as Ferrere offer advisory work. The external audit is a separate paid service. The competitor check was limited by budget, so regional AML vendors are not ruled out.
result.duty: Res 201/20 SEPRELAD, in force since Sep 2020, sets the rules for anyone who regularly buys or sells property: agencies, agents, brokers, commission agents and developers. It requires a compliance officer (the owner can hold the role in a one-owner firm), a manual, a code of ethics and a risk assessment at least every 2 years, with the method checked every 4 years. Customer checks are simplified below thresholds of 150 minimum wages paid at once or 20 minimum wages a year in instalments, and customers on freeze lists must be screened. An annual internal evaluation goes to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end, an external audit report within 180 days, and a negative report for every 3-month period with no ROS. SEPRELAD resolutions from April to July 2023 moved real-estate ROS and negative reports to SIRO, so the claim's ROS-WEB/Res 94/19 basis is superseded. The 2023 SIRO resolutions also cover NGOs, cash-in-transit and safe-deposit firms, payment firms and gambling operators, and the Feb-Mar 2023 ones cover notaries, car dealers, remitters, political organizations and pawn shops. Penalties: Ferrere mentions only 'significant' financial and reputational penalties; no amounts found. I did not verify the Ley 6960/2022 amendment. A July 2026 Ultima Hora page says SEPRELAD is studying stricter sector rules for real estate, but its date is doubtful because it describes 2019 events.
result.market: Not found. No count of registered real-estate agencies with SEPRELAD was found. The only registry figure found was 6,262 registered non-profits (2022, prensamercosur), with almost 4,000 more said to be unregistered. Treating this as one product across the separate sector rulebooks (real estate, pawn shops, NGOs and others) is unverified; each sector has its own resolution, so separate vertical templates are likely.
result.reason: The duty is real and heavier than the claim says, but the claim's legal basis is out of date. SEPRELAD Res 201/20 (14 Sep 2020) repealed Res 264/07 and 266/07 for real-estate agencies, agents, brokers and developers. It requires a compliance officer, an AML manual, a code of ethics and a risk assessment every 2 years. It also requires KYC above set thresholds, an annual internal evaluation sent to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end, an external audit within 180 days, and a negative report for any 3 months with no ROS. Since 2023, reports go through SEPRELAD's free SIRO system, not ROS-WEB. I found no private software. Weak points: penalty amounts and agency count not found, likely low willingness to pay, and accountants already sell the audit service.

Duty is real: Ley 3369/07 (amending 2716/05) requires a DISA non-theft report and a Certificado de Baja y Desarme from the Registro de Automotores. Art. 7 covers those who sell or transport used parts as a main or secondary activity. Enforcement is active: police raided clandestine dismantlers in Asunción and Villeta on 31 Jul 2026 for lacking sale documents. I found no Paraguayan digital platform or competitor, but I did not search thoroughly for one. Weaknesses: a small, informal market with no register count found, clandestine operators who avoid compliance, a per-vehicle workflow set by the state, and no evidence of penalty amounts or frequency. I could not confirm the law's current text or any later decrees. Not read: Art. 7 details.

The duty exists but sits on concessionaires, not on small agencies or sub-agents. Ferrere says concessionaires must keep a detailed register of bets taken, prizes paid, unpaid and unclaimed. It gives no filing frequency or penalty. Concessions are limited to about three per vertical, so the buyer pool is tiny and concentrated. Sports betting online is held by Daruma SAM (Apostala) until 2028. Slot-hall decree text requires an on-site online monitoring system with CONAJZAR access, so the state or its vendor covers the core job. I found no register of small operators and no sub-agent duty. I did not check competitor software. Bingo is reported as unregulated. Weak SME fit.

The duty is real. BCP Res 7/19 and SB.SG 132/19 created the register for habitual money lenders, cheque discounters and credit houses. SEPRELAD Res 55/2020 ended the old registration, and the BCP Superintendencia now supervises AML for them. Res 30/2022 adds public transparency duties (website disclosure of fees), effective 1 Sept 2022. These are administrative offences under Law 489/95 as amended by Law 6104/18. I found no recurring periodic filing to the BCP, and no software vendor or free state tool for it. The bcp.gov.py page returned 403, so periodic reporting stays unchecked. Registration is largely one-off and the market is small (358 in 2022; the 30.04.2026 PDF list was unreadable). That means weak recurrence and a thin MVP. Generic loan software exists (Loandisk, CrediManager) but none was confirmed as Paraguay-specific. Not enough evidence to confirm the claim, but a score of 2 reflects a weak candidate.

The duty is real. Ley 422/73 and Decreto 11681/75 require INFONA guides for transporting and selling wood and forest products. Charcoal is covered, and sawdust and carbonilla need subproduct guides plus Registro Público Forestal de Comercio enrolment. Ley 6616/2020 and INFONA Res. 116/2021 add an export registry for exotic-species logs and billets. The guide duty applies to every shipment, so it recurs. Competition: INFONA runs its own digital system. A UNDP-sourced note says it covers guide issuance, forest registry and traceability, so a state tool already does the core job. A third-party tool would have to integrate with it, and no private API was found. Market: charcoal is about 10,000 t a year and total forest exports were USD 100.6M in 2025. No count of firms was found, and the buyers are informal and low-paying. I could not open the INFONA portal, so the online procedure is unverified.

Duty is real: the press describes a plan de fuego before purchase, SID registration of coded units, and Digemabel Res. 260/2026 (18 Jun 2026). It sets mandatory in-person oversight of every blast in Ita, Emboscada and San Lazaro, plus purchase restrictions. I did not open or find the resolution text, so deadlines, penalties and SID fields are unchecked. Searches found no private Paraguayan software for this. But SID is the state system and the controls are tightening. The market is about 151 quarries, mostly informal, with one SID user each. Buyers are few and poor, and the Senate may ease the rules. The product would only mirror SID. Willingness to pay is low and the market is tiny, so the score is low.

Ley 5424/15 is real: the Policía Nacional licenses agencies and issues guard credentials, and an estimated 300 firms operate unlicensed (La Nación 2022). Articles 31, 33 and 35 appear in DNCP tender answers. I did not read the statute, so periodic filing duties, penalties and the current bill status are unconfirmed. Two searches found no Paraguayan guard-compliance product, only foreign generic guard software (C-Guard Pro, ShiftFlow, Guardhouse, ProxiGuard). The market is small, with 135-252 licensed agencies. No Policía digital filing workflow was confirmed, which weakens the "mandatory recurring filing" case. The product would overlap with generic shift and payroll tools, and K10/K12 rejected the payroll angle. Score stays at 4.
